title: Staged multi-region failover choreography and dry-run harness for Private VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Private (VPC) customers expect documented, repeatable multi-region recovery drills that can be executed with minimal ops intervention and provide measurable validation of application-level readiness. Current artifacts are ad-hoc: a mix of manual runbooks and per-customer scripts. This initiative builds a reusable choreography and a dry-run harness that can execute full failover rehearsals (no-ops dry runs and live toggles) across customer-private VPC deployments using Terraform-based IaC and light orchestration wrappers. The goal is a single, configurable set of modules and a lightweight coordinator that performs preflight validations, staged promotion, canary traffic shepherding, post-cutover health checks, and automated rollback on detected regressions.
background: We already maintain Terraform modules for Private deployments and a few tooling scripts used during customer cutovers. Customers have requested predictable rehearsal capabilities to satisfy compliance reviews. Previous tickets have focused on terraform orchestration and simulated failover (see related tickets), but none provide a reusable sequencer that embeds application-level probes and dry-run gating. This ticket addresses that gap by defining choreography and implementing a dry-run harness that integrates with existing IaC.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Terraform module (drill_choreography) that can be included into customer Private stacks to provision the orchestration primitives (SQS/SNS or equivalent, controller IAM roles, optional Lambda hooks) and wiring for pre/post hooks

A coordinator binary (or lightweight Lambda) that, given a drill plan, runs a staged rehearsal: preflight -> canary promotion -> progressive traffic shepherd -> post-cutover validation -> rollback if failure
Dry-run mode that simulates the flow without making live routing changes but validates all preflight checks and runbook steps
End-to-end drill can be triggered from Redwood Console UI and via CLI (terraform apply wrapper or api request) with proper RBAC checks

Health checks include both infra-level (KV cache presence, disk space, node readiness) and app-level (sample prompt latency, response schema check, model checksum match). Failure thresholds are configurable per-customer
Run results are emitted to Console metrics and a drill report stored in customer S3/log sink with timestamps and artifacts (terraform plans, diagnostics, failing probe logs)
Automated rollback executes within policy windows and leaves clear post-mortem artifacts; manual abort and forced-promote are supported via API with audit logging
implementation_notes: Design will use a small coordinator service implemented as either a Fargate task or Lambda that accepts a JSON drill plan. Terraform module will expose resources and wiring only — it will not run the drill. The coordinator will call existing control plane APIs for model routing and region promotion. Preflight checks will include: terraform plan dry-run for infra changes, KV key hold-check, live smoke prompt to a pinned model version, and a checksum of model artifacts in the target region. For live drills, traffic shepherding will be accomplished via staged routing percentages (0 -> 10 -> 50 -> 100) with per-step wait windows and golden metrics gating (95th p90 latency, error rate, hallucination rate from baseline eval set). The dry-run harness will stub routing API calls and still run probes and terraform plan to validate IaC changes. We will reuse per-customer KMS/HSM roles for signing and per-drill locks in the infra to avoid concurrent drills. The terraform module will support parameterization for promoted-traffic-duration, canary-size, rollback-thresholds, and observability endpoints.

T2: Terraform module dr_choreography: resources, IAM, SQS topics, lock TTLs (Marco) - 3d
T3: Coordinator prototype (lambda/fargate) with dry-run and live modes (Samantha) - 5d
T4: Integrate health probes: sample prompt harness + schema validator + model checksum (Applied ML) - 4d
T5: Console integration: trigger button and drill records view (Frontend) - 3d
T6: CI tests: unit tests for coordinator + terraform plan smoke tests + integration test harness (Infra QA) - 4d
T7: Run three internal rehearsals across synthetic customers, capture metrics and iterate (All) - 2d
T8: Docs: runbook, run checklist, incident/rollback playbook, customer-facing how-to (Docs) - 2d
risks: Risk of accidental traffic promotion if coordinator bug introduces a race; mitigations include terraform-managed locks, immutable promotion tokens, and a mandatory dry-run before first live drill. Another risk is noisy canary metrics causing false rollbacks; we will use baseline windows and configurable thresholds per-customer.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: please validate the proposed gating metrics for p95 latency and hallucination detection thresholds. The coordinator will require auth scopes to mutate routing — suggest we scope to project-level role and require an approval step in Console for first-time rollout per-customer.
